name: Abebe Bikila
one_line: PART 2: Forty days after surgery he won the Olympic marathon again - then lost his legs, and kept competing anyway.

facts.claim: 40 days before the 1964 Tokyo Olympic marathon, Bikila had an appendectomy
facts.note: Part 2 opens here. He was not expected to be fit.

facts.claim: he won Tokyo 1964 in 2:12:11.2 - another world record - finishing 4 minutes and 8 seconds ahead of silver medalist Basil Heatley
facts.note: Wearing shoes this time (Puma). The 4:08 margin is enormous for an Olympic marathon.

facts.claim: the first person in history to win the Olympic marathon twice
facts.note: Wikipedia: 'First athlete to successfully defend an Olympic marathon title.' Chart: gold 2 vs gray 1 = the most by anyone before him.

facts.claim: in March 1969 his car overturned near Addis Ababa; he was paralyzed and never walked again, though he regained upper-body mobility
facts.note: Volkswagen, 22 March 1969. Tone: state it plainly, no melodrama - the channel's deadpan carries grief better than adjectives.

facts.claim: he kept competing: archery and table tennis at the 1970 Stoke Mandeville Wheelchair Games, and won a cross-country sled event in Norway in 1971
facts.note: THE part-2 beat: the man who ran barefoot found new sports from a wheelchair - and won again (Norway sled, 1971).

facts.claim: died October 1973, aged 41, of a cerebral hemorrhage related to the accident; an estimated 65,000 people attended his state funeral and Haile Selassie declared a national day of mourning
facts.note: The national stadium in Addis Ababa bears his name.

comparison.second_label: the most by anyone before him
comparison.gap_description: The first person ever to win the Olympic marathon twice - 40 days after surgery.

story_beat: Forty days after an appendectomy, Bikila won the Tokyo Olympic marathon by over four minutes - the first person ever to win it twice. Five years later a car crash took his legs. He switched to archery, then sled racing - and won in Norway in 1971. He died at 41; sixty-five thousand people came to say goodbye.
